372 journal prompts for mental health

A prompt is a door into a page you would not otherwise have written. These 372 are the ones Theraglee gives its members, one a day: gratitude, stress, relationships, what you are proud of, what you are avoiding. Read them here, pick one, and write.

How to use a journal prompt

Pick the prompt that makes you pause, not the one that looks easiest. Set a small limit, five minutes or one page, so starting is not a commitment. Write the way you talk, without fixing spelling or finding the right word, and keep the pen moving even if what comes out is "I do not know what to write about this."

When the time is up, read it back once. You are looking for the sentence that surprised you, because that is the one worth returning to tomorrow.

Start a private journal, free One prompt a day on your dashboard, nothing shared.

Common questions

Do I need an account to use these prompts?

No. Every prompt is on this page. A free Theraglee account adds a private journal on your dashboard with one prompt a day, your earlier entries, and search across them. It never asks for a card.

Is journaling a form of therapy?

No. Writing can help you notice what you think and feel, and many people find it steadying, but it is not treatment and it does not replace a licensed therapist. If what comes up worries you, the therapist directory is free to browse.

How long should I write for?

A few minutes is plenty. Pick a prompt, write until you run out of things to say, and stop. Short, honest and regular does more than long and occasional.

Who can read my journal on Theraglee?

Only you. Journal entries stay in your own account. Therapists never see them, including when Theraglee Match Mode is switched on, and Theraglee never sells or shares what you write.
